instruction: I have three images available on the Desktop: pic2.png, pic4.png, and pic6.png. Create a new presentation with exactly three blank slides (no text boxes or other content), then insert pic2.png on the first slide, pic4.png on the second slide, and pic6.png on the third slide. This will be used for a kiosk display.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires creating 3 blank slides and inserting pic2.png, pic4.png, and pic6.png (every other image from the original set). Expected: 3 slides total, each with exactly 1 image. Similar complexity to original task but with fewer slides.

llm_judge_reasons: CRITICAL: Evaluator cannot verify WHICH specific images were inserted (pic2.png, pic4.png, pic6.png). It only checks that 3 images exist, not their identities or filenames.

CRITICAL: Evaluator cannot verify the ORDER of images. Instruction requires pic2.png on slide 1, pic4.png on slide 2, pic6.png on slide 3, but evaluator cannot distinguish this from wrong orderings (e.g., pic6, pic2, pic4).

CRITICAL: Evaluator cannot verify 'blank slides' requirement. Instruction explicitly requires 'no text boxes or other content', but evaluator only counts images and ignores text boxes, shapes, or other unwanted content.
The evaluator would incorrectly pass if: (1) wrong images were inserted (e.g., pic1, pic3, pic5), (2) correct images in wrong order, or (3) slides contain text boxes or extra shapes.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Getter should extract image metadata including filenames/image data from each slide to verify specific images (pic2.png, pic4.png, pic6.png) are used.
Getter should extract images in slide order and verify: slide 1 has pic2.png, slide 2 has pic4.png, slide 3 has pic6.png.
Getter should count ALL shape types per slide (text boxes, shapes, etc.) to verify slides are truly 'blank' except for the required images.
Metric should compare extracted image identifiers against expected images per slide: {'slide_1_image': 'pic2.png', 'slide_2_image': 'pic4.png', 'slide_3_image': 'pic6.png'}.
Consider using image hash comparison or filename extraction from PPTX relationship files to identify specific images.
